title: The Geometry of LLM-as-Judge: Why Inter-LLM Consensus Is Not Human Alignment
reasoning: The paper focuses on the geometric alignment and scoring consistency of LLMs acting as judges compared to human evaluators. While it uses cultural and medical advisory datasets that involve human values and includes isolated factual questions about religious history (e.g., Sikhism in Table 11), it does not explicitly benchmark moral reasoning, ethical frameworks, or religious belief systems as a core component of the study.
